recent_commits.message: Teams notification survives quotes in the commit message (0.4.0.1)
recent_commits.body:
The workflow pasted the commit message into a single-quoted shell string,
so an apostrophe ("main's") ended the string and the step failed, and the
rest of the message was run as shell code. The message now reaches the
shell as an environment variable and jq writes the JSON; curl --fail makes
a refused webhook show as a failed step.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

files.patch:
@@ -9,10 +9,16 @@ jobs:
   notify:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
+      # The commit message reaches the shell as an environment variable and jq
+      # writes the JSON, so quotes, apostrophes and line breaks in it can no
+      # longer break the command (an apostrophe made this step fail), and no
+      # part of it is run as shell code.
       - name: Send notification to Teams
+        env:
+          TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.

recent_commits.message: code_read() stops on an HTTP error again instead of reading the error page as code (0.4.0.11)
recent_commits.body:
The new code_read() (#513) fetches a URL with curl::curl_fetch_memory(),
which does not fail on an HTTP error, so a missing file's error page was
read as its code: a github.com 404 gave 682 lines of HTML. readLines() used
to stop there, and code_check recorded the file as not read. code_read()
now stops with "cannot open URL '<url>': HTTP status was <n>" for a status
of 400 or above. The manifest test in test-module-code_check.R no longer
expects the warning readLines() used to give.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Merge dev into report-checklist (0.4.0.11 after #514's 0.4.0.10)
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #513 from scienceverse/fix/code-read-crash
recent_commits.body: code_read() no longer crashes R on an undefined byte (#511)
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: module_find() searches installed modules before the working directory (0.4.0.10)
recent_commits.body:
A file modules/<name>.R in the working directory replaced the installed
module <name>, so a server running a check from inside an uploaded folder ran
the upload's code. Built-in modules, then installed ones, then the working
directory and its modules/ folder. Fixes #512.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: code_read() no longer crashes R on an undefined byte (0.4.0.9)
recent_commits.body:
readr::read_lines() in the guessed encoding crashed R (vroom segfault while
unwinding from "Invalid multibyte sequence") on a byte that encoding leaves
undefined, such as 0x81 in windows-1252. code_read() now reads the bytes and
converts them with iconv(sub = "byte"), in the same guessed encoding. Fixes #511.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Package layout: rewrite only paths that cannot work, writes stay in place (0.4.0.8)
recent_commits.body:
- A relative path that names no file from the top or from the script's
  folder is left as written (code joins it with a folder of its own; the
  rewrite doubled it: processed_data/fig7/processed_data/fig7/x.csv). A path
  relative to the script's folder goes to the file's path from the top; an
  absolute path or one out of the package is rewritten by file name.
- Writes stay where the code puts them, so later scripts find the files;
  only writes to absolute paths or out of the package go to output/.
- The copied files and folders are writable, so a script can save over a
  file the package holds (the Docker sandbox runs as another user).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check runs a local folder's code in a copy of the package (0.4.0.7)
recent_commits.body:
- New argument layout: "package" copies every file to its own path, so code
  that reads folders or imports its own modules finds them; only a path that
  does not work there is rewritten, a path that works is left as written.
  "auto" (default) uses it for a local folder (local_path), and the Psych-DS
  layout otherwise, as before. Each script is written to, and each file
  copied from, its own path, so files with the same name no longer collide.
- A Python file other files import is not run as a script of its own
  (outcome run_by_import), like an R script another script source()s.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Checklist report; Python advice in code_check; OSF token and ResearchBox downloads fixed (0.4.0.6)
recent_commits.body:
- report_type("checklist"): a fifth report type that sorts every check of
  every module into to fix, to improve, decide by hand, for information,
  fine and not applicable, with what was found and what to do on separate
  lines, in the colours and font of metacheck's website. A module can give
  its checks as a `checks` data frame (plus `intro` and `logo`); others are
  shown as one check. New R/report-checklist.R and
  inst/templates/_report_checklist.Rmd; the module "How It Works" text moves
  to .report_how_it_works(); collapse_section() folds in this report type.
- A static table cell starting like a list item ("1. GENERAL INFORMATION")
  no longer opens a list that swallows the rest of the report.
- code_check gives Python code Python advice on package versions
  (requirements.txt and similar are found; .code_env_pinned()).
- OSF downloads with an OSF token no longer send the token to the storage
  host, and work again since the OSF moved to Oracle storage (#508).
- ResearchBox downloads send the new text file ids.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #510 from scienceverse/fix/report-other-disk
recent_commits.body: report() saves the report when the output file is on another disk (0.4.0.5)
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: report() saves the report on another disk too (0.4.0.5)
recent_commits.body:
report() renders in R's temporary folder and moved the result with
file.rename(), which cannot move a file to another disk: it returns
FALSE without an error, so the output file kept the "test" that
report() writes to check the path. On the SURF API, whose job folders
are on a storage volume, an installed module's report came back as
"test". .report_move() copies the file when renaming fails, and stops
with an error when that fails too.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #509 from scienceverse/external-modules
recent_commits.body: Modules from GitHub, junk files and the file tree, SURF conversion, data_check and code_check fixes (0.4.0.4)
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Convert PDFs on SURF by default; data_check reads every same-named file; code_check names local files (0.4.0.4)
recent_commits.body:
- convert_bibr() gets backend = "surf" (metacheck's API on SURF Research
  Cloud, no key needed), used by "auto" unless a Scienceverse key or a bibr
  address is given; SURF_API_URL sets its address. The server's reason is
  passed on when a conversion fails, DOC/DOCX are refused before sending,
  and the file name the server reports (input.pdf) is replaced by the real
  one. convert() asks SURF first (checked with .surf_isalive()), then falls
  back to the old order.
- data_check kept each table under its file name alone, so same-named files
  in different folders replaced each other (4 of 46 tables checked in a
  measurement package). Files now get a unique source_file
  (.data_source_keys()): the name, else the path, else repository + path;
  previews, columns, findings and codebook_check's labels use it.
- code_check's report table showed NA for the names of local files (a link
  to a missing web address); it now shows their path.
- Help pages regenerated (three were out of date with their source).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Show everything in the file tree; classify licences, models, .vcd, .pgf and package lists (0.4.0.3)
recent_commits.body:
- File tree: a local folder is listed itself, with hidden files, junk files
  and empty folders; a repository link also shows repo_check's junk files.
  Marks: "junk: remove", "junk: keep only on purpose" (a junk folder is one
  line with its number of files), "hidden file", "empty folder". Folders,
  empty ones included, before files. The tree sits in a scroll box, and the
  repository apps show it open instead of folded. data_check passes
  repo_check's useless_files to it.
- Classifier: LICENSE/LICENCE/COPYING without extension -> documentation
  (licence role); .slx and .mph -> code; .vcd -> data; .pgf -> output;
  requirements*.txt and Pipfile -> code
- .mc_request() moved above .batch_query()'s roxygen block, so it no longer
  takes over that help page
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: repo_check flags junk files as TU/e's data managers do; share the file tree (0.4.0.2)
recent_commits.body:
- .useless_file_kind() adds the junk rules of TU/e's data managers: editor
  backups (file~, .bak, .swp, .swo), temporary files (.tmp, .temp),
  .Rhistory, .TemporaryItems and every ~$ lock file as problems; version
  control (.git, .svn, .hg) and editor settings (.idea, .vscode) as
  suggestions (.useless_file_severity())
- repo_check: a problem kind turns the light red, a suggestion kind yellow;
  the files are returned as useless_files (paper_id, repo_url, file_path,
  kind, severity), and the report says which to remove and which to keep
  only on purpose
- local_files() lists hidden files of these kinds (.DS_Store, .Rhistory,
  .git/), so repo_check finds them in a local folder too
- R/file-tree.R: data_check's file tree (.file_tree_rows(),
  .file_tree_block()) moved into the package, with .file_tree() for the
  repository apps' brief report and external modules; the apps no longer
  keep their own copy
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Install modules from GitHub with module_install() (0.4.0.1)
recent_commits.body:
- module_install("owner/repo", ref) downloads a repository into the
  metacheck user data folder (or METACHECK_MODULES_DIR); every .R file
  with a roxygen header in its top folder or modules/ becomes a module
  that module_run(), report(), module_info() and module_help() find by
  name. Nothing is saved when a name is already used by a built-in
  module, another installed repository, or twice in the same repository.
  A module can state its lowest metacheck version (#' @metacheck x.y.z),
  checked by module_install() and module_run().
- module_update(), module_remove() and module_installed()
- module_list() lists installed modules, with their repository in a new
  source column; module_list(external = FALSE) lists built-in ones only
- report: an installed module's How It Works names its repository and
  commit instead of linking to a manual chapter
- test-module-repo_check.R: the three summary tables include the
  repo_unchecked column added in c5c98a1
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Show a reproducibility check that ran code in the brief report, also when green (0.3.3.19)
recent_commits.body:
report_qmd() kept only red/yellow/fail modules in brief mode, so a
reproducibility check whose scripts all ran (green) disappeared. A module
can now set brief = TRUE in its output to be kept whatever its light;
reproducibility_check does when it ran at least one script (#504).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Redirect script writes to output/ relative to the sandbox root, so they work in Docker (0.3.3.18)
recent_commits.body:
repro_write_scripts() replaced {{REPRO_OUTPUT}} with file.path(root,
"output"), an absolute host path; the Docker sandbox mounts root at
/sandbox, so every script that wrote a file failed inside the container.
The replacement is now "output/", which works in both sandboxes since
every script runs with the sandbox root as working directory (#502).
New tests: the rewritten path is relative, and a script writing a file
runs in a Docker container and its file reaches the host's output/.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Report OSF links that could not be checked; name uploaded zips by their folder in the repository check app (0.3.3.17)
recent_commits.body:
- .osf_parse_response() gives each failed lookup a reason in an `error`
  column (HTTP 503 -> osf_type "error", "the OSF API did not answer";
  404/410 "unfound" with their own reason; 429), so it is not cached on disk;
  osf_info() no longer keeps failed lookups in its session cache (#501)
- repo_check keeps OSF links that could not be looked up, with their reason
  in gated_repos, instead of removing them with the registrations (#501)
- repo_check's summary and report name repositories that could not be
  checked instead of counting them as empty or without README (all
  platforms); the light is not green then; new repo_unchecked column
- Repository check app: an uploaded zip is unpacked into a folder named
  after it and checked from the folder above, so the report shows its name,
  not the server's temporary path (#500); new test-app-repocheck.R
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Accept .NET multipart uploads in the plumber API; refuse JSON that is not bibr output (0.3.3.16)
recent_commits.body:
- plumber API: parse_upload() reads the request body with
  webutils::parse_http() (plumber's own parser) instead of
  mime::parse_multipart(), which only recognised a part whose
  Content-Disposition header came first; .NET's MultipartFormDataContent
  (PowerShell, C#) writes Content-Type first, so its uploads and form fields
  were lost. Same returned shape, endpoints unchanged (#498)
- .read_bibr() stops with "is not bibr output (it has no paper_id)" for a
  JSON file without a paper_id; read() skips it with a warning. module_run()
  keeps the module's own error when paper_id() fails in its handler (#499)
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Give repository requests a stall guard; ask zip_peek for the exact central directory (0.3.3.15)
recent_commits.body:
- .mc_request(): httr2::request() with curl's low-speed limit (< 1 KB/s
  for 60 s) and a 30 s connect timeout, used by the 38 repository and
  database requests that had no time limit (zip listing, GitHub, GitLab,
  OSF, ResearchBox (300 s), PsychArchives, DSpace, AsPredicted, FSD,
  DataONE, Dryad, CrossRef, PubPeer, Retraction Watch, RegCheck status,
  paper corpora, prereg_check's schema). Not used for LLM, GROBID, bibr or
  upload requests, whose servers work before answering (#473)
- zip_peek(): after a first tail too short for the central directory, the
  second request asks for the bytes the end record says it needs
  (.parse_zip_central_dir(need_only = TRUE)), up to 64 MB, instead of a
  fixed 1 MB
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Unpack only kept archive files within max_file_size in data_check (0.3.3.14)
recent_commits.body:
- .archive_keep(): the keep rule of .archive_rows() (data, code, README and
  codebook documentation, not skip_types or useless files), applied to an
  archive's listing before anything is unpacked
- .expand_compressed() decompresses a .gz/.bz2/.xz only when the inner file
  is kept, and stops at max_bytes (partial copy deleted); .expand_zip() and
  .expand_tar() unpack only kept members within max_bytes (sizes from the
  zip listing or tar headers; a compressed tar's are checked after
  unpacking). Files over the limit are listed without a copy and added to
  data_check's oversize record; copies over the limit from earlier runs are
  removed (#472)
- .rate_limit_wait test allows a few seconds instead of an exact rounded 900
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: power: free-text categories mapped onto known values, report unchecked paragraphs, require ellmer 0.4.2 (0.3.3.13)
recent_commits.body:
- The LLM answers power_type, statistical_test, effect_size_metric and
  software as free strings; .power_canonicalise() maps them onto the known
  values, keeping an unmatched answer in *_other (new software_other). A
  value outside a type_enum() made Groq reject the whole call (POWSIM)
- The software list holds 116 power/sample-size packages from CRAN's
  package list, 10 widely used ones whose title does not say so, 6 no longer
  on CRAN or from Bioconductor, and other software (POWSIM, nQuery, SAS, ...)
- Paragraphs the LLM could not check are counted and reported (summary,
  report, yellow light, power_unchecked per paper) instead of being counted
  as having no power analysis
- DESCRIPTION: ellmer (>= 0.4.2)
- The Ollama structured power test also replaces ellmer::chat_vllm(), used
  since #494 (#475)
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Keep the report header for a paper without a title or DOI; close <col> tags in the simple report (0.3.3.12)
recent_commits.body:
- report(): an NA title, or a missing doi field, fills its header placeholder with nothing. sub() with an NA replacement returned NA for the whole header (YAML, CSS, banner and info box became "NA"), and a zero-length replacement stopped report() with "invalid 'replacement' argument" (#497) - report_table(): column widths are written as ; Pandoc read the unclosed as an open element, lost the simple report's page
and left a stray
recent_commits.author: Lakens

_new_commits.body:
The new code_read() (#513) fetches a URL with curl::curl_fetch_memory(),
which does not fail on an HTTP error, so a missing file's error page was
read as its code: a github.com 404 gave 682 lines of HTML. readLines() used

now stops with "cannot open URL '<url>': HTTP status was <n>" for a status

expects the warning readLines() used to give.

_new_commits.body:
A file modules/<name>.R in the working directory replaced the installed
module <name>, so a server running a check from inside an uploaded folder ran
the upload's code. Built-in modules, then installed ones, then the working
directory and its modules/ folder. Fixes #512.

_new_commits.message: code_read() no longer crashes R on an undefined byte (0.4.0.9)
_new_commits.body:
readr::read_lines() in the guessed encoding crashed R (vroom segfault while
unwinding from "Invalid multibyte sequence") on a byte that encoding leaves
undefined, such as 0x81 in windows-1252. code_read() now reads the bytes and
converts them with iconv(sub = "byte"), in the same guessed encoding. Fixes #511.

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Divide whole numbers with plain floor() and ceiling()
recent_commits.body:
* floor_div() and ceiling_div() checked floor(a / b) by multiplying it back out. Below 2^53, IEEE 754 division already makes floor(a / b) exact for whole numbers, so the check never fired. Above 2^53 the products round too, and in a random sample of 200,000 cases the check broke correct results about 14 times as often as it repaired wrong ones.

* Every call site now uses floor() or ceiling() directly; the reasoning is in the comment at the top of R/unround.R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give a value that would look like a bound just enough places
recent_commits.body:
* format_number() fell back to 12 significant digits for a value that
would look whole or like a bound, e.g. 0.146504464074. It now adds the
fewest decimal places that set the value apart, e.g. 0.146504.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that explain_map()'s data was tested with formula = "mean_n"
recent_commits.body:
* Through explain_map(), debit_explain()'s own check said `formula` is
"mean_n", though the user never passed `formula`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make unexplainable GRIMMER reasons an internal error
recent_commits.body:
* "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding bounds undefined" can't happen,
and explain_undecidable() has no words for them: it said the number of
items had to be a positive whole number, but was 1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't show DEBIT's example SD as an excluded bound
recent_commits.body:
* Picking the k closest to the middle of the range didn't help when only
one k passes: debit_explain(0, sd = 0.147, n = 320, digits_x = 1,
digits_sd = 3, rounding = "down") showed an SD of 0.1465 as in a range
above 0.1465. format_number() now takes the bounds a value is compared
to and shows it in more detail if it would look like one of them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Share explanation helpers with the tests they explain
recent_commits.body:
* spread_out_most() gives the values behind sum_squares_scale_max() to
both it and describe_spread_out(), and binary_spread_root() the root
behind binary_sd_attainable() to both it and binary_ones_shown().
* debit_explain() gets a `formula` argument that rejects "mean_n", so
explain_map() no longer has to know what the explainer can't do.
* Align the pipes in the mapper-tier test.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't blame the scale for a GRIMMER range that was already empty
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_candidate() applied the scale ceiling even when the sum of
squares range held no whole number without it, so the reason became
"scale range" instead of "test 1", and grimmer_explain() said the
ceiling was "too small" rather than that the range was empty.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show rounding bounds in full at 4+ decimal places
recent_commits.body:
* format_number() rounded to 4 places, so the bounds of a value reported
with 4 or more decimals were cut off, and describe_range() could then
call an interval a single point. It now shows `digits + 2` places, at
least four.
* grimmer_explain() routes the "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding
bounds undefined" reasons to explain_undecidable() rather than letting
them reach the candidate loop with an NA verdict.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let explain_map() dispatch on any class
recent_commits.body:
* The class check ran in the generic ahead of `UseMethod()`, so no method
for another class could ever be reached. It is `explain_map.default()` now,
with the same error, and `explain_print()` only checks for a tibble before
slicing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pass explain_map() rows as plain vectors
recent_commits.body:
* `explain_row()` subset the tibble with `data[i, cols]` per row. It now
indexes a list of the columns, which saves about 6% on a 932-row
`grim_map_seq()` output; the rest is the `*_explain()` calls themselves.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write GRIMMER explanations only for candidates that are shown
recent_commits.body:
* The loop built a paragraph for every failing candidate sum and then kept
the first three. It now counts the failures after the third without writing
them out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Share DEBIT's bounds with debit_explain() and stop listing every k
recent_commits.body:
* `debit_bounds()` clamps the mean's and the SD's rounding bounds once, for
`debit_scalar()` and `debit_explain()` alike, so the text can't drift from
the bounds that decided the test.
* `debit_explain()` listed every number of ones from `sum_lower` to
`sum_upper`, millions for a large `n`. `binary_ones_shown()` finds the few
the text needs next to the roots of `k * (n - k) = spread`; a brute-force test
checks it against the full list.
* The example `k` is now the passing one whose SD is closest to the middle of
the range. The smallest one sat at a bound, and once rounded for display, its
SD could read as exactly the bound the text had just excluded.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write out large numbers in explanations
recent_commits.body:
* `paste()` wrote round numbers like 100000 as 1e+05 in the text and in the
header. Each `*_explain()` function now raises `scipen` while it runs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain a missing `items` value instead of erroring
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_explain()` and `grimmer_explain()` tested `items != 1` for the
header, which failed on `NA`, so one such row aborted `explain_map()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pick explain_print() rows like dplyr::slice() and check for mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print(data, ...) passes the dots to dplyr::slice() instead of
  taking `n`, so any rows can be printed, not just the first ones.
* explain_map() and explain_print() call check_explainable(), which
  requires output of grim_map(), grimmer_map(), or debit_map() (or
  their sequence and total-n mappers) instead of failing in dispatch.
* The re-test error names the row by its values, not by a position that
  slice() or filter() had already shifted.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain_print() and rename the `text` element to `paragraphs`
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() prints the `explanation` column of mapper output,
  optionally only the first `n` rows. Without the column, it calls
  explain_map() on these rows only, so the others are not re-tested.
* The `text` element of `scrutiny_explain` objects is now `paragraphs`,
  which is harder to mix up with `test`.
* Blank lines between the steps of the longer explain functions, and
  Lukas's pipe and control-flow edits to R/grim-explain.R.
* The explain sweep test uses one decimal count and fewer sample sizes,
  cutting test-explain.R from 18 to 7.5 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Store explain_map() output in a column and flatten the explain helpers
recent_commits.body:
* explain_map() returns its input with an `explanation` column of
  format()ed explanations instead of a list; format.scrutiny_explain()
  replaces print.scrutiny_explain_list(). explain_rows() becomes
  add_explanation_col().
* grimmer_explain() reuses grim_explain() for the GRIM part, and the
  single-use grim_explain_text(), grimmer_explain_text(),
  debit_explain_text(), summarize_candidates(), and describe_parity()
  are inlined into their callers.
* describe_reported() replaces describe_digits() and the four copies of
  the sentence on a reported value's rounding range.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename explain() to explain_map() and mark verdicts with ==>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` is also exported by DALEX and lime, which would mask it,
and reusing dplyr's generic did not help against them. `explain_map()`
is a scrutiny generic like `audit()`, so the dplyr re-export and the
`name_data` argument of `check_cols_needed()` are gone.

* `=>` read like the `>=` operator.

* `explain_rows()` pipes the row indices into a separate
`explain_row()` instead of nesting an anonymous function.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add explain() for mapper output and mark verdicts with =>
recent_commits.body:
* `explain()` methods for `grim_map()`, `grimmer_map()`, and `debit_map()`
output, which also covers the seq and total-n tiers. Each row is tested
again from its values plus the settings in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
a verdict that differs from the row's `consistency` is an error.

* The generic is `dplyr::explain()`, re-exported, so attaching both
packages masks nothing.

* `check_cols_needed()` takes the name of the data argument, which is `x`
for S3 methods of a dplyr generic.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_explain(), grimmer_explain(), and debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Each tests a single case and lays out the calculation in plain words,
from the rounding bounds of the reported values to the verdict.

* GRIM's text comes from `grim_scalar(show_rec = TRUE)` plus
`bound_numerators()`. GRIMMER's and DEBIT's come from the helpers their
tests use, and abort if their reading disagrees with the verdict; a sweep
in test-explain.R exercises that check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Factor GRIMMER's candidate test and DEBIT's spread range into helpers
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer_sd_bounds()` and `grimmer_candidate()` hold the SD bounds and
the per-candidate tests 1 and 3; `binary_spread_range()` holds the spread
bounds of `binary_sd_attainable()`. The explain functions reuse them, so
their text cannot drift from the verdict.

* About 6% slower on `grimmer()` from the extra call per candidate sum.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Attribute #86 to GRIMMER in the unround.R header comment
recent_commits.body: * GRIM never derived its candidate sums from floating-point products; it rounded the two nearest granules forward and compared them with a tolerance, so its released versions were not affected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check needed columns in audit() and grim_plot(); fall back to rounding
recent_commits.body:
* Mapper output keeps its class after columns are dropped, so audit() and
  grim_plot() failed with unclear errors. A shared check_cols_needed() now
  names the missing columns; grim_plot_rates() and debit_plot() use it too.
* grim_plot() uses its rounding argument when data has no recorded
  rounding method, as with a hand-built tibble.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Map grim_plot() value-set colors to a scale and drop four style arguments
recent_commits.body:
* consistency is mapped to colour and fill of the value-set tiles, with one default scale for both, as in debit_plot(); adding another scale restyles them.
* color_cons, color_incons, tile_alpha, and raster_alpha are removed. tile_size and raster_color stay: no scale reaches them, and raster_color also builds the gradient for three or more decimal places.
* The in-depth vignette's plotting requirements now describe the scale instead of color arguments.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test check_audit_special() and manage_helper_col()
recent_commits.body:
* Both are exported for handwritten mappers but had no tests of their own.
* check_audit_special() is tested on basic, seq, and total-n output; manage_helper_col() on a column, an argument, the default, affix = FALSE, and the conflict error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

repos.readme_excerpt:
**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

docpluck turns a research article into text you can run statistical checks on. It extracts the
text layer, repairs the damage extraction itself causes (lost minus signs, split ligatures,
interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

highlights.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
highlights.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
highlights.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
highlights.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
highlights.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
highlights.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.

highlights.body: Modules from GitHub, junk files and the file tree, SURF conversion, data_check and code_check fixes (0.4.0.4)
highlights.author: Daniel Lakens

highlights.message: Convert PDFs on SURF by default; data_check reads every same-named file; code_check names local files (0.4.0.4)
highlights.body:
- convert_bibr() gets backend = "surf" (metacheck's API on SURF Research
  Cloud, no key needed), used by "auto" unless a Scienceverse key or a bibr
  address is given; SURF_API_URL sets its address. The server's reason is
  passed on when a conversion fails, DOC/DOCX are refused before sending,
  and the file name the server reports (input.pdf) is replaced by the real
  one. convert() asks SURF first (checked with .surf_isalive()), then falls
  back to the old order.
- data_check kept each table under its file name alone, so same-named files
  in different folders replaced each other (4 of 46 tables checked in a
  measurement package). Files now get a unique source_file
  (.data_source_keys()): the name, else the path, else repository + path;
  previews, columns, findings and codebook_check's labels use it.
- code_check's report table showed NA for the names of local files (a link
  to a missing web address); it now shows their path.
- Help pages regenerated (three were out of date with their source).
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Show everything in the file tree; classify licences, models, .vcd, .pgf and package lists (0.4.0.3)
highlights.body:
- File tree: a local folder is listed itself, with hidden files, junk files
  and empty folders; a repository link also shows repo_check's junk files.
  Marks: "junk: remove", "junk: keep only on purpose" (a junk folder is one
  line with its number of files), "hidden file", "empty folder". Folders,
  empty ones included, before files. The tree sits in a scroll box, and the
  repository apps show it open instead of folded. data_check passes
  repo_check's useless_files to it.
- Classifier: LICENSE/LICENCE/COPYING without extension -> documentation
  (licence role); .slx and .mph -> code; .vcd -> data; .pgf -> output;
  requirements*.txt and Pipfile -> code
- .mc_request() moved above .batch_query()'s roxygen block, so it no longer
  takes over that help page
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: repo_check flags junk files as TU/e's data managers do; share the file tree (0.4.0.2)
highlights.body:
- .useless_file_kind() adds the junk rules of TU/e's data managers: editor
  backups (file~, .bak, .swp, .swo), temporary files (.tmp, .temp),
  .Rhistory, .TemporaryItems and every ~$ lock file as problems; version
  control (.git, .svn, .hg) and editor settings (.idea, .vscode) as
  suggestions (.useless_file_severity())
- repo_check: a problem kind turns the light red, a suggestion kind yellow;
  the files are returned as useless_files (paper_id, repo_url, file_path,
  kind, severity), and the report says which to remove and which to keep
  only on purpose
- local_files() lists hidden files of these kinds (.DS_Store, .Rhistory,
  .git/), so repo_check finds them in a local folder too
- R/file-tree.R: data_check's file tree (.file_tree_rows(),
  .file_tree_block()) moved into the package, with .file_tree() for the
  repository apps' brief report and external modules; the apps no longer
  keep their own copy
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Install modules from GitHub with module_install() (0.4.0.1)
highlights.body:
- module_install("owner/repo", ref) downloads a repository into the
  metacheck user data folder (or METACHECK_MODULES_DIR); every .R file
  with a roxygen header in its top folder or modules/ becomes a module
  that module_run(), report(), module_info() and module_help() find by
  name. Nothing is saved when a name is already used by a built-in
  module, another installed repository, or twice in the same repository.
  A module can state its lowest metacheck version (#' @metacheck x.y.z),
  checked by module_install() and module_run().
- module_update(), module_remove() and module_installed()
- module_list() lists installed modules, with their repository in a new
  source column; module_list(external = FALSE) lists built-in ones only
- report: an installed module's How It Works names its repository and
  commit instead of linking to a manual chapter
- test-module-repo_check.R: the three summary tables include the
  repo_unchecked column added in c5c98a1
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Divide whole numbers with plain floor() and ceiling()
highlights.body:
* floor_div() and ceiling_div() checked floor(a / b) by multiplying it back out. Below 2^53, IEEE 754 division already makes floor(a / b) exact for whole numbers, so the check never fired. Above 2^53 the products round too, and in a random sample of 200,000 cases the check broke correct results about 14 times as often as it repaired wrong ones.

* Every call site now uses floor() or ceiling() directly; the reasoning is in the comment at the top of R/unround.R.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Give a value that would look like a bound just enough places
highlights.body:
* format_number() fell back to 12 significant digits for a value that
would look whole or like a bound, e.g. 0.146504464074. It now adds the
fewest decimal places that set the value apart, e.g. 0.146504.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Say that explain_map()'s data was tested with formula = "mean_n"
highlights.body:
* Through explain_map(), debit_explain()'s own check said `formula` is
"mean_n", though the user never passed `formula`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Make unexplainable GRIMMER reasons an internal error
highlights.body:
* "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding bounds undefined" can't happen,
and explain_undecidable() has no words for them: it said the number of
items had to be a positive whole number, but was 1.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Don't show DEBIT's example SD as an excluded bound
highlights.body:
* Picking the k closest to the middle of the range didn't help when only
one k passes: debit_explain(0, sd = 0.147, n = 320, digits_x = 1,
digits_sd = 3, rounding = "down") showed an SD of 0.1465 as in a range
above 0.1465. format_number() now takes the bounds a value is compared
to and shows it in more detail if it would look like one of them.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Share explanation helpers with the tests they explain
highlights.body:
* spread_out_most() gives the values behind sum_squares_scale_max() to
both it and describe_spread_out(), and binary_spread_root() the root
behind binary_sd_attainable() to both it and binary_ones_shown().
* debit_explain() gets a `formula` argument that rejects "mean_n", so
explain_map() no longer has to know what the explainer can't do.
* Align the pipes in the mapper-tier test.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Don't blame the scale for a GRIMMER range that was already empty
highlights.body:
* grimmer_candidate() applied the scale ceiling even when the sum of
squares range held no whole number without it, so the reason became
"scale range" instead of "test 1", and grimmer_explain() said the
ceiling was "too small" rather than that the range was empty.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Show rounding bounds in full at 4+ decimal places
highlights.body:
* format_number() rounded to 4 places, so the bounds of a value reported
with 4 or more decimals were cut off, and describe_range() could then
call an interval a single point. It now shows `digits + 2` places, at
least four.
* grimmer_explain() routes the "GRIM undecidable" and "SD rounding
bounds undefined" reasons to explain_undecidable() rather than letting
them reach the candidate loop with an NA verdict.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Show a reproducibility check that ran code in the brief report, also when green (0.3.3.19)
highlights.body:
report_qmd() kept only red/yellow/fail modules in brief mode, so a
reproducibility check whose scripts all ran (green) disappeared. A module
can now set brief = TRUE in its output to be kept whatever its light;
reproducibility_check does when it ran at least one script (#504).
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Redirect script writes to output/ relative to the sandbox root, so they work in Docker (0.3.3.18)
highlights.body:
repro_write_scripts() replaced {{REPRO_OUTPUT}} with file.path(root,
"output"), an absolute host path; the Docker sandbox mounts root at
/sandbox, so every script that wrote a file failed inside the container.
The replacement is now "output/", which works in both sandboxes since
every script runs with the sandbox root as working directory (#502).
New tests: the rewritten path is relative, and a script writing a file
runs in a Docker container and its file reaches the host's output/.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Report OSF links that could not be checked; name uploaded zips by their folder in the repository check app (0.3.3.17)
highlights.body:
- .osf_parse_response() gives each failed lookup a reason in an `error`
  column (HTTP 503 -> osf_type "error", "the OSF API did not answer";
  404/410 "unfound" with their own reason; 429), so it is not cached on disk;
  osf_info() no longer keeps failed lookups in its session cache (#501)
- repo_check keeps OSF links that could not be looked up, with their reason
  in gated_repos, instead of removing them with the registrations (#501)
- repo_check's summary and report name repositories that could not be
  checked instead of counting them as empty or without README (all
  platforms); the light is not green then; new repo_unchecked column
- Repository check app: an uploaded zip is unpacked into a folder named
  after it and checked from the folder above, so the report shows its name,
  not the server's temporary path (#500); new test-app-repocheck.R
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Accept .NET multipart uploads in the plumber API; refuse JSON that is not bibr output (0.3.3.16)
highlights.body:
- plumber API: parse_upload() reads the request body with
  webutils::parse_http() (plumber's own parser) instead of
  mime::parse_multipart(), which only recognised a part whose
  Content-Disposition header came first; .NET's MultipartFormDataContent
  (PowerShell, C#) writes Content-Type first, so its uploads and form fields
  were lost. Same returned shape, endpoints unchanged (#498)
- .read_bibr() stops with "is not bibr output (it has no paper_id)" for a
  JSON file without a paper_id; read() skips it with a warning. module_run()
  keeps the module's own error when paper_id() fails in its handler (#499)
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Give repository requests a stall guard; ask zip_peek for the exact central directory (0.3.3.15)
highlights.body:
- .mc_request(): httr2::request() with curl's low-speed limit (< 1 KB/s
  for 60 s) and a 30 s connect timeout, used by the 38 repository and
  database requests that had no time limit (zip listing, GitHub, GitLab,
  OSF, ResearchBox (300 s), PsychArchives, DSpace, AsPredicted, FSD,
  DataONE, Dryad, CrossRef, PubPeer, Retraction Watch, RegCheck status,
  paper corpora, prereg_check's schema). Not used for LLM, GROBID, bibr or
  upload requests, whose servers work before answering (#473)
- zip_peek(): after a first tail too short for the central directory, the
  second request asks for the bytes the end record says it needs
  (.parse_zip_central_dir(need_only = TRUE)), up to 64 MB, instead of a
  fixed 1 MB
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Unpack only kept archive files within max_file_size in data_check (0.3.3.14)
highlights.body:
- .archive_keep(): the keep rule of .archive_rows() (data, code, README and
  codebook documentation, not skip_types or useless files), applied to an
  archive's listing before anything is unpacked
- .expand_compressed() decompresses a .gz/.bz2/.xz only when the inner file
  is kept, and stops at max_bytes (partial copy deleted); .expand_zip() and
  .expand_tar() unpack only kept members within max_bytes (sizes from the
  zip listing or tar headers; a compressed tar's are checked after
  unpacking). Files over the limit are listed without a copy and added to
  data_check's oversize record; copies over the limit from earlier runs are
  removed (#472)
- .rate_limit_wait test allows a few seconds instead of an exact rounded 900
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: power: free-text categories mapped onto known values, report unchecked paragraphs, require ellmer 0.4.2 (0.3.3.13)
highlights.body:
- The LLM answers power_type, statistical_test, effect_size_metric and
  software as free strings; .power_canonicalise() maps them onto the known
  values, keeping an unmatched answer in *_other (new software_other). A
  value outside a type_enum() made Groq reject the whole call (POWSIM)
- The software list holds 116 power/sample-size packages from CRAN's
  package list, 10 widely used ones whose title does not say so, 6 no longer
  on CRAN or from Bioconductor, and other software (POWSIM, nQuery, SAS, ...)
- Paragraphs the LLM could not check are counted and reported (summary,
  report, yellow light, power_unchecked per paper) instead of being counted
  as having no power analysis
- DESCRIPTION: ellmer (>= 0.4.2)
- The Ollama structured power test also replaces ellmer::chat_vllm(), used
  since #494 (#475)
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Keep the report header for a paper without a title or DOI; close <col> tags in the simple report (0.3.3.12)
highlights.body:
- report(): an NA title, or a missing doi field, fills its header placeholder with nothing. sub() with an NA replacement returned NA for the whole header (YAML, CSS, banner and info box became "NA"), and a zero-length replacement stopped report() with "invalid 'replacement' argument" (#497) - report_table(): column widths are written as ; Pandoc read the unclosed as an open element, lost the simple report's page
and left a stray
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Let explain_map() dispatch on any class
highlights.body:
* The class check ran in the generic ahead of `UseMethod()`, so no method
for another class could ever be reached. It is `explain_map.default()` now,
with the same error, and `explain_print()` only checks for a tibble before
slicing.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Pass explain_map() rows as plain vectors
highlights.body:
* `explain_row()` subset the tibble with `data[i, cols]` per row. It now
indexes a list of the columns, which saves about 6% on a 932-row
`grim_map_seq()` output; the rest is the `*_explain()` calls themselves.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write GRIMMER explanations only for candidates that are shown
highlights.body:
* The loop built a paragraph for every failing candidate sum and then kept
the first three. It now counts the failures after the third without writing
them out.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
